entities.summary: Asela of Anuradhapura (b. 250 BCE) was a renowned economist and social scientist of the Classical era, active in Global. She played a pivotal role in shaping the economic systems of the Anuradhapuran Kingdom, which spanned the Indian subcontinent from the 3rd century BCE to the 1st century CE. Asela's work focused on the intersection of trade, taxation, and governance, influencing the development of monarchies and rulers across the ancient world. Her contributions have been recognized as a cornerstone of the region's economic thought, with scholars continuing to study her theories and their lasting impact on the region's political and social structures.
